messages:
alicia: seeing a sudden spike in privileged session activity in the audit stream — starting ~03:12 UTC. opening this thread to coord. usernames: svc-data-processor, deployer-bot. suspected lateral use.
sec-bot: [ALERT] privileged_session_anomaly detected, score=0.92, sessions=178 in 6m, kinesis/audit_stream: /prod/auth/events. related_kms_decrypts=42. links: https://siem.internal/redwood/alerts/1988887776
 tom: can you paste the quick query for the hits? I want to know source IPs and services touched.
 alicia: pasted below — filtering on service_account, event=CreateSession / AssumeRole / KMS:Decrypt.
 ```sql
 SELECT src_ip, service, actor, COUNT(*) as cnt
 FROM audit_events
 WHERE event IN ("AssumeRole","CreateSession","KMS:Decrypt")
   AND ts > 1672531200
 GROUP BY src_ip, service, actor
 ORDER BY cnt DESC
 LIMIT 50;
 ```
 raj: ran that, top sources are 3 IPs from a colo range (54.86.23.0/24), actors show repeated service-account usage for svc-data-processor, and there are 8 unique deployments that triggered KMS decrypts. attaching brief output: `54.86.23.17 -> svc-data-processor -> 62` `54.86.23.18 -> deployer-bot -> 49` `54.86.23.21 -> svc-ml-ingest -> 31`
 maria: I rotated the short-lived session tokens for svc-data-processor and blocked those three IPs at the edge. commands run:
 ```bash
 # revoke sessions
 aws sts revoke-session --session-id <id>
 # rotate svc keys (temp)
 gcloud iam service-accounts keys create /tmp/newkey.json --iam-account=svc-data-processor@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
 # edge block
 iptables -I INPUT -s 54.86.23.0/24 -j DROP
 ```
 dmitri: good. any signs of data exfil? KMS decrypt count spiked but do we have S3/DB download activity correlated?
 alicia: we cross-checked S3 access logs — only 3 downloads from svc-data-processor in that window; sizes small (<200KB) but there are multiple KMS decrypts tied to internal config blobs. no obvious bulk exfil.
 tom: I'm going to triage RBAC mappings. if the service account had over-permissive roles recently, that could explain lateral. who changed bindings in last 48h?
 raj: iam_audit shows a role-binding change by deployer-bot at 02:47 UTC adding roles/storage.objectViewer to svc-data-processor for a short-lived rollout. looks like an automated PR bot created it. PR id: 4142.
 maria: rolling back that binding now and creating a scoped role for the job.
 alicia: note: preserve evidence — snapshot audit db and timestamped logs (I exported /prod/auth/events to s3://sec-evidence/1988887776/)
 sec-bot: [ACTION] evidence snapshot stored: s3://sec-evidence/1988887776/ (sha256: 3a7f...)
 dmitri: handing off to night oncall. summary for follow-up: 1) blocked suspect IP range; 2) rotated keys/sessions for affected SAs; 3) revoked temporary role added by deployer-bot; 4) no large data exfil detected but KMS decrypt pattern suspicious — escalate to IR for deeper forensic on deployer-bot and build pipeline. please pick this up and run full container image scan + CI token audit.
 alicia: creating follow-up ticket and tagging sec/ir and eng-platform. ticket: SEC-2026. brief entry: "Privileged session surge from colo IPs, temporary RBAC elevation by deployer-bot, KMS decrypt spike; containment applied; forensics pending."
 tom: assign to dmitri and eng-platform@lists. next steps: verify build pipeline creds, check PR 4142 for CI token usage, run yara scan on pulled images.
 dmitri: ack, will pick up at 03:35 UTC. leaving notes here for continuity. :white_check_mark:
 alicia: thanks team — closing war-room thread, will update incident timeline in postmortem channel after IR completes. :thumbsup:
